topics.label: Introduction to the lecture and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines the objectives of the final lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and systemic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional therapeutic approaches—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapeutics—alongside their mechanisms of action and clinical limitations.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities, checkpoint defects, and DNA repair pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit distinct biological vulnerabilities in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint alterations, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the development and application of small-molecule kinase inhibitors targeting driver oncogenes, as well as the pathways and challenges of acquired drug resistance.

topics.label: Therapeutic monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on engineered antibody technologies designed to bind tumor-associated surface antigens and deliver targeted cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunology, checkpoint inhibition, and adoptive cell therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the biological basis of tumor immunosurveillance and the application of immunotherapies, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific engagers, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Clinical challenges, historical trends, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize broad clinical considerations in oncology, spanning genomic stratification, epidemiological trends, treatment challenges, and ethical considerations.
